title: Paris Blues soundtrack
summary: He doesn't recall Paris Blues but remembers Murray McEachern and extracting the parts recorded in California.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: How about Paris Blues?
Pardon me?
Paris Blues? Remember the film, Paris Blues? Duke did that in 1961.
That's far back for me.
1961? He got an Academy Award nomination for the score on that one.
Who did?
Duke.
Duke?
Yeah. With Paul Newman and Joanne Woodward and Sidney Poitier and Dianne Carroll were in the film. And it was made in France.
Well, if they made that in France, I don't know anything about it.
But you're on the soundtrack.
Maybe they made those things and he didn't even know they were making them -- that's what I'm saying.
And Paul Newman is supposed to play a Murray McEachern trombone player and Marin Mcgeford played the trombone parts for him in the film.
Who was it?
Paul Newman.
Paul Newman was the star of this Murray McEachern film, playing the role of a trombone player and Marin Mcgeford did the soundtrack of what Paul Newman was supposed to play.
I do believe I remember something like that. I remember that trombone player -- what was his name?
Murray McEachern.
Murray McGrekin. Yeah, he played a solo on something in the studio. We were making the picture, yeah, and we were doing the recording on it.

Yeah. And the music score was Billy Byers by Duke Ellington, and supervised by Billie Beyers, the jazz sequences by Louie Armstrong. The controversy rages as to which musicians are responsible for individual sequences, but Paul Gonsalves Gonzalez and Murray McEachern ghosted McGrekin goes to the two principals. So I guess when Paul played for what? Sidney Poitier? I can't remember the story now.
